hypothesis: If domestic dogs descend from several distinct wild species, then genome-wide sequence data from dogs should show that dog lineages trace to two or more separate wild canid species (for example wolf, jackal or coyote), not to one species.
pass_criterion: Using the dog reference genome, aligned to genomes of Canis lupus, C. latrans, C. aureus and other Canis species, at least two deeply diverged dog lineages are sister to different wild species. Alternatively, a non-wolf species contributes at least 10% of dog ancestry, with ABBA-BABA D-statistics giving |Z| > 3 across breeds. Either result counts as support for multi-species descent.
fail_criterion: Dogs form a single monophyletic clade nested within Canis lupus in at least 95% of 100-kb autosomal windows. Any non-wolf species contributes under 5% of ancestry, with no significant D-statistic (|Z| < 3). That result refutes descent from several distinct wild species and supports a single-species (wolf) origin.
interpretation: Darwin's 'wild species' is read as a modern biological species of Canis (wolf C. lupus, golden jackal C. aureus, coyote C. latrans, and others). His 'descended from' is read as ancestry detectable in genome-wide phylogeny and admixture statistics. Gene flow between wolves and dogs after domestication does not count, because it involves the same species, C. lupus. A modern reinterpretation applies: dogs are classed as C. lupus familiaris, so 'several species' can only be supported by a non-wolf species contributing ancestry. Limitation: the chosen portal page is the dog reference assembly. The comparison canid assemblies and reads would have to be pulled from the same NCBI portal, and no single dataset record contains them all. The test is therefore only as complete as that retrieval.

dataset.name: Canis lupus familiaris genome assembly UU_Cfam_GSD_1.0 (GCF_011100685.1)
dataset.why_it_fits: This is the dog reference genome on NCBI Datasets, with downloadable FASTA and GFF files and an API. Its fields are chromosome sequences and annotations. Aligned with other Canis assemblies and population reads from NCBI, they allow window-based phylogeny and D-statistics for the pass/fail test.
